Water-libation, salutation!"
Then, one should pray for the food offering (naivedya).
O Lord, let the command be given to me to partake of this food offering.
You ought to act so that the maintenance of my body may be accomplished.
Then, one should cast flowers into the water jar.
I have fallen into distress; you are my refuge. I am in every state at all times.

O Blessed One, I have taken refuge in you; protect me who have come for shelter. Indeed, [I am burdened by] sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, as well as approaching those with whom one should not have sexual intercourse.
The drinker of intoxicants, the thief, the killer of an embryo, the violator of the guru’s bed, the stealer of gold or land, the slayer of a cow, and the murderer of a father.
The matricide, the killer of a woman, the slayer of a guru, and all other sins whatsoever—other terrible deeds committed in three ways by the thousands.
By remembering Amṛteśa, all doubts are reduced to ashes; even those who have committed a hundred murders perish [through this], so what need be said of a killer of a Brahmin?
O Śivā, by the power of this mantra, all those mantras that consist of seven crores and hundreds of repetitions become as if already recited.

Whatever merit is found in the four Vedas, whatever fruit is obtained from all sacrifices, and whatever majesty resides in all sacred fords—that shall be attained by reciting [this mantra] one hundred times.
O Goddess of the gods, when [the deity] is worshipped before Śiva with a hundred recitations, a mortal shall enjoy the fruit of liberation in a single birth.

O slender-limbed one, a mantra-reciter who is constantly disciplined and pure-minded should perform the recitation one hundred and eight times; he is equal to a perfected being—of this there is no doubt.
O beautiful lady, he in whose heart this [mantra] abides, being ever disciplined, uplifts ten generations of his ancestors and ten generations of his descendants.
O lady of excellent vows, death does not afflict him who, though seized by time, constantly remembers [this] at the three junctions of the day, wherever he may be situated;
he does not fall under the power of death, nor of disease, nor of thieves. By merely worshipping it once, harmful beings and the like are indeed destroyed.
Just as deer flee from a lion, they vanish in all eighteen directions; through the practice of those virtuous ones, poverty is destroyed from the family.
In whatever country and at whatever time a knower of mantras may dwell, there shall be no calamities, diseases, droughts, thieves, or malevolent planets.
Various Śākinīs, Yakṣas, Piśācas, Rākṣasas, and Āgrahas; Bālagrahas, Visphoṭakas, Vyantaras, and those that dwell within.
All varieties of poison, the affliction of famine, and everything else have no power at all in the presence of one who knows this mantra.
Having always honored all living beings and kings alike, if one honors them with gifts, worship, and equal treatment, then they will be truly honored.
By merely honoring him, all mantras become honored; they bestow happiness there, so one should worship them through him as their mouth.
For the planets, which everywhere cause severance, afflict the practitioner; therefore, one should always offer the planets the release of water.
The desired planets are satisfied; once satisfied, they indeed do not exert their influence. Enough with further elaboration; these flowers are worthy of acceptance.
Now follows the Bhairava-samayā.

The seer (ṛṣi) of this mantra is Kahāla; the meter (chandaḥ) is Gāyatrī; the deity (devatā) is Mṛtyuñjaya. Oṃ juṃ saḥ! To the one whose form is nectar, who pervades the sky, whose body is the void—ward off the violation of all commitments (samaya)! Ward them off twice! Fulfill the commitment! Fulfill it twice!

To the one whose mantra-body is common to all, O Immortal One, O Supreme Immortal One, O Eternal One, hrīṃ svāhā! Homage to you, O Lord of the Skull, who are eternally worshipped by the King of the Gods.
O best of Bhairavas, O devotee of Śiva, accept this worship and protect me.
O Lord of Bhairavas, homage to you, O consumer of oblations, who are fully worshipped and a devotee of Śiva. || 2 ||
Homage to you, O King of Wrath, who are worshipped by Vaivasvata; O devotee of Śiva! 3.

O Vikarāla, homage to you, who are eternally worshipped by Nairṛta; O devotee of Śiva! 4 O Manmatha, homage to you, who are worshipped by Varuṇa; O devotee of Śiva! 5 O Meghanāda, homage to you, who are worshipped by Prabhañjana; O devotee of Śiva! 6 O Somarāja, homage to you, who are eternally worshipped by the Lord of Yakṣas; O devotee of Śiva! 7 O Vidyārāja, homage to you, who are eternally worshipped by Rudra; O devotee of Śiva! 8

We praise Svacchanda Bhairava, whose body is the light of the city [of the senses], who is the single form of the universe, the self of the universe, and the cause of the creation and other states of the universe.
We praise Svacchandabhairava, who transcends the universe yet consists of the universe, who is joined with the eight Bhairavas, who is both with parts and without parts, and who is peaceful.
Salutations to that Aghora, whose very self is more terrible than the most terrible.
To the supreme Lord, who consists of the five Brahmās, together with his limbs and attendants, for the sake of the causes of creation, sustenance, withdrawal, dissolution, and grace.
I seek forgiveness from Maheśvara, along with his manifestations and his powers. O twelve-fold soul, salutations to you; salutations again and again to Mārtāṇḍa.
O Maker of Day, grant protection to one bitten by the serpent of disease!
O Lord of Rohiṇī, marked by the spot of the night's lord (the hare), salutations to you; O Maker of Night, grant protection to me who am scorched by the poison of saṃsāra. || 2 ||
O Aṅgāraka, salutations to you, the warder-off of all suffering; O Son of the Earth, grant protection to this wretched and impoverished man.
O son of Soma, salutations to you; salutations to the king of the planets.
O son of Rohiṇī, grant peace to one who is submerged in the mire of existence! (85b)4)
O Vācaspati, Preceptor of the Gods, salutations to you; protect me. Be ever gracious toward me, a sinner devoid of wisdom. || 5 ||

Obeisance to you, the son of the Sun, the preceptor of the enemies of the gods; you are supreme compassion. Having removed the afflictions caused by the planets within the periods and so forth, protect me, O Lord of Light.
Salutations to the one whose body is dark; O son of the Sun, salutations be unto you! O Śanaiścara, grant protection to me who am terrified by the fear of saṃsāra.
O son of Siṃhikā, salutations to you; ward off the affliction of the planets. O Vidhuntuda, grant protection to me who am scorched by the fire of suffering. 8.
May the Sun and the other planets, including Ketu, who are devoted to the worship of Śiva, protect the dharma, lifespan, friends, and sons of the patron.
Now follows the "Forgiveness of the World Protectors."
O Blessed One, O King of Gods, I have exhausted you at this sacrifice; accept my worship, O Lord of Gods, and may it be forgiven, may it be forgiven, O Master! (1)
"O Blessed One, O Blessed One, O Fire-god, you have been distressed by me at this sacrifice; accept this worship, O Lord of Gods, and may it be forgiven, may it be forgiven, O Lord."
O Lord of the Yoni, you have been defeated by me in the sacrifice; accept this worship of Śiva, O Master, may you forgive me, may you forgive me.
O Blessed One, protector from destruction and from the terrible ocean of saṃsāra, I am weary; O Lord, depart now to your own abode.
O Blessed One, since you have been worshipped as Śrī Śiva at this sacrifice by Varuṇa and others, O God, I have been wearied by you; I shall now go to my own purifying abode.
"O Blessed One, O Bhavagant, you have been wearied by me in this Śāmbhava sacrifice; having accepted my worship, go now to your own abode as you please."
O Lord of the Phallus, you have not been harmed during this sacrifice to Śaṅkara; having taken the image offered by me, may you forgive me, may you forgive me, O Lord! (7)
O Blessed One, God of gods, you yourself [performed] the worship of Īśāna in your own sacrifice.
"Having taken it, grant me all human goals and then depart. (8)
O Blessed One, worthy of worship by the three worlds, Grandfather of all the worlds! Protection was indeed provided for this sacrifice by you; therefore, O Lord, may it be forgiven.
O Blessed One, O Blessed Viṣṇu, O destroyer of the Dānavas! You have provided protection during this sacrifice to Śiva; therefore, O Lord, may it be forgiven.
May all the blessed planets and those who are considered secondary planets accept this worship offered by me; being satisfied, may they depart to their own abodes.
O Blessed One, Lord of the Skull, you who were worshipped with the discus when I was greatly distressed during the Śaiva sacrifice—O Bhairavendra, salutations to you!
O Lord who rides upon the peacock, you who were worshipped by me at the sacrifice Śāṅkara, having been propitiated, you have indeed returned to your own abode satisfied.

O Blessed One, you who are the King of Wrath (Krodharāja), whose nature is dharma, and who are honored through sacrifice; having performed protection at the Śaiva ritual, you have indeed reached your own stainless state.
O Blessed One, you who are eternally worshipped by Nirṛti, O Vikarāla, accept this Śaiva worship which leads to your own stainless state. 4.
O Blessed One, Lord of my mind, whose worship was performed by Varuṇa; O Lord, this Yakṣa has been distressed during the sacrifice to Śiva—may he be forgiven.
O Lord Meghanāda, O sinless one, you have been honored by Vāyu; you were distressed during the Śaiva sacrifice—forgive me, forgive me, O Lord! (6)
O Blessed One, King Soma, honored by the gods and the givers of wealth; O Lord, you who have provided protection at the sacrifice of Śiva, may you forgive us, may you forgive us! (7)
O Lord, King of Knowledge, you have been invoked today in this Śaiva sacrificial rite; O Divine One, may you forgive us, may you forgive us, O Lord! (8)
Those beginning with Ananta who reside within this sevenfold enclosure—may they all, being honored and satisfied, proceed to the supreme state of Śiva.
O Śambhu, O Lord of the auspicious world, O Blessed One, I have been wearied by me.
You are the god of the gods of gods; you alone are the supreme refuge.
You are the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, and the cause of all causes. When you are pleased, all the gods are pleased; may they be forever well-disposed toward us.
Mounted upon Airāvaṇa, golden-hued and of great splendor, the Lord of the Devas is ever contented and devoted to the supreme worship.
Constantly devoted to meditation on Śiva, permeated by the true nature of Śiva, and supreme in his prostrations to Śiva—may he grant me peace. || 1 ||
The god Agni brings prosperity to embodied beings and is the destroyer of sins; he is intent upon the worship of Śiva and the recitation of mantras, and is permeated by the true nature of Śiva.
May the Lord grant me peace as well as the complete destruction of my sins. || 2 ||
May Antaka, who possesses great splendor and is solely devoted to the meditation on Śiva, being engaged in the worship of Śiva, grant me well-being and health. || 3 ||
The lord of the Rākṣasas, Nirṛti, who is eternally devoted to the worship of Śiva, may he grant me great peace, being ever eager for devotion to Śiva. || 4 ||
May Varuṇa, whose mind is solely intent on Śiva through supreme devotion, forever destroy for me the torment of the fires of disease and grief. || 5 ||
May the supreme deity Pavana, who is meditated upon as the Supreme Lord, constantly grant me well-being, health, strength, and peace. || 6 ||
May Kuvera, the bestower of boons, the glorious one who delights in the worship of Hara’s feet, being pleased and tranquil, grant me peace with his peaceful splendor. May he grant me peace. 7.
Īśāna is the supreme deity, the highest among all the best of gods; may he too, through his nature as the self of all, swiftly grant me peace. || 8 ||
May those who dwell in the earthly realm (Bhūloka), the intermediate realm (Bhuvarloka), and the heavenly realm (Svarloka)—the gods endowed with divine splendor—grant me peace forever. 9.
May those gods who dwell in the Mahāloka, Janaloka, and Tapaloka also, being greatly delighted, always bestow peace upon me. 10.
And those gods in Satyaloka, whose bodies are radiant with their own splendor, who are devotees of Śiva and pure-minded—may they utterly destroy my fear. || 11 ||
Whether committed by hand or foot, born of speech or body, arising from the ear or born of the eye or hearing—O Mother, may there be no offense whatsoever.
Forgive all of this, whether it was done according to rule or not; victory, victory to you, O Śambhu, the Great Lord, ocean of compassion!
Forgive me, O Lord of Mantras, who consists of eternal bliss, for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, and so that you may return again.

Forgive whatever I have done that was deficient or excessive; O you whose form is the universe, reveal yourself! Be gracious, O Lord of Gods; salutations to you! Depart satisfied, so that you may return again.
He who is the one God, all-knowing, the witness of the entire universe’s action, who is inaccessible even to Brahmā and the other gods, and who was worshipped with equanimity in the sacrifice;
The Lord is both with parts and without parts, established in the station of the twelve-finger space; that divine Śambhu has been propitiated in this ritual procedure.

Śambhu, who alone is capable of performing creation, preservation, and destruction, who possesses three forms and three qualities—having been worshipped according to the rule by Śvakhā—[attains his purpose].

By this God of gods, who is devoid of qualities and whose form is the Self, that Śakti was worshipped according to the rule (samaya) at the sacrifice, having been approached through the threefold means.
Today my birth has become fruitful; today my actions have become fruitful, since Śambhu, who possesses such power, has been distressed at this sacrifice for Śiva.
O protector of the gods, save me, who am helpless amidst this sinful calamity; grant me success, prosperity, wisdom, and mental purity.
Grant me both worldly enjoyment and liberation as desired by my mind; O Great Lord, grant me eternal perfection in all things.
O Śambhu, O Supreme Lord, grant me the state free from affliction. Now, O Supreme Ruler, O Lord, may you forgive me, may you forgive me.
"You have been invoked in this sacrifice; being satisfied, go indeed to your own abode. Gaṇeśa and the others who were remembered here for the duty of guarding the door [should likewise depart]."
Indra and the other guardians of the world, as well as the Ādityas and the other planets; and those who begin with Ka, the Bhairavas who reside here supported by the Bhairavīs within the skull.
The mantras of the seven coverings, as well as the deities of the garments and so forth; likewise, the collection of the six paths and the deities beginning with Gāyatrī.
The deities of the planets and other gods, beginning with Vāstoṣpati; the Vaṭukas, Herukas, and others; and the eternal guardians of the fields (kṣetrapālas).
May they all, having bestowed various boons, return to their own abodes. I do not know invocation at all; I do not know worship at all.
I do not know the ritual of dismissal; may it be forgiven, O Supreme Lord.
With both knees, hands, head, and chest, I perform salutation; homage! "Homage to Brahman," and so forth.

One should meditate on the various mantras as having entered within the mantra-pitcher like sparks, into that light which was previously established. That mass of light residing in the pitcher, in the form of the Lord Bhairava with all his aspects (*sakalabhairava-bhaṭṭāraka*), should be dissolved by the Goddess of Withdrawal (*saṃhāriṇī*) into the Lord without parts (*niṣkalanātha*).

He too, by the process of upward emission, [dissolves] into the *bindu*; the *bindu* into the *nāda*; the *nāda* into the *śakti*; and she too, by the method of cessation, into the half-moon (*ardhacandra*) and the obstructress (*nirodhinī*), until [all] are pervaded.

One should contemplate that [the deity] has dissolved into one's own nature through the process of the dissolution of the mantra; the all-pervading consciousness-form is the supreme mantra-splendor: *oṃ juṃ saḥ*, *saḥ juṃ oṃ*.
I merge this into my own self; *namaḥ*.

Thus, having grasped [the breath] with the twelve-finger span of the *bhoga* and brought it to the heart by means of inhalation (*pūraka*), one should worship there according to the method of salutation; so say the Gurus.
Then, one should recite the Melāpa-vidyā three times.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ saḥ saḥ, O bestower of happiness and good fortune, O Haṃsa, O Mistress of Speech! Come, come! Haṃsa 2, be present, be present! O bestower of all prosperity, O warder-off of all evil, O subjugator of the entire world, [for those who are] divided... p. 88)
Bring about the union of the mantras, twice; may there be grace for me! Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Saḥ Saḥ Hūṃ Hūṃ.
Now follows the mantra for forgiveness.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ strīṃ prīṃ jyaṃ! O Lord of the six flavors of the Supreme Sovereign, you who enter the abode of the pure nectar of all commitments, grant your presence here; dry up the sins of body, speech, and mind; cause expansion in the heart; effect purification of the heart; dispel the arrogance of those who worship [only] gods; abide in my body; O dweller in the seven netherworlds and the serpent-abodes, who carry both the gross and the subtle!
HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
Arise, arise, O Lord of Gods, together with the deities of the maṇḍala! You who are known as Tatpuruṣa, protect us eternally from the east.
Likewise, protect from the south; you are Śaṅkara, the God of gods. Constantly stationed in the direction of Varuṇa, may Sadyojāta protect me.
Protect me above, O Maheśāna; you are the Lord, the deity. In every way, at all times, O God, [protect me] everywhere on this path of worldly existence.
Protect me, O Lord of Gods, for [I seek] that state which consists of eternal bliss.
Having recited the hymn beginning with "brahmādi," one should bathe the patron, together with his retinue, with the water from the mantra-pitcher or with the water from the arghya vessel.
May the gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—consecrate you; as well as Vāsudeva, the Lord of the World, and the sovereign Saṅkarṣaṇa.
May Pradyumna and Aniruddha be for your victory! May Ākhaṇḍala, Agni, the Lord Yama, and likewise Nairṛta [be your protectors].
Varuṇa, Pavana, Vadhana, Adhikṣa, and likewise Śiva.
Śeṣa, together with Brahmā, and the guardians of the quarters, always offer him praise.
Fame, Fortune, Conduct, Intelligence, Nourishment, Faith, Forbearance, Intellect, Modesty, Body, Peace, Praise, and Beauty are the Mothers.
May these wives of Dharma, having assembled together, consecrate you: Āditya, Candra, Bhauma, Ābhauma, Budha, Jīva, Śita, and Arkaja.
May the planets consecrate you—Rāhu and Ketu being gratified—as well as the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas.
The ṛṣis, the munis, the cows, and the mothers of the gods; the wives of the gods, the dhruvas, the nāgas, the daityas, and the hosts of apsarases.
All missiles, all weapons, kings, vehicles, medicinal herbs, jewels, Mount Kailāsa, and those who are the winds.
May the rivers, oceans, mountains, sacred fords, and clouds consecrate you for the fulfillment of all desires and purposes.
May the meanings of the mantras be fruitful; may all desires be fulfilled; may there be the destruction of the intellect of enemies; and may we praise the prosperity of friends.
Thus, the fire-ritual (agnikārya) is completed in this brief sequence. Saṃvat 16, on the second day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, on a Thursday.

Oṃ. Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme characteristics of sacrificial animals: those that are white and black are the best, while those that are variegated and pale yellow are middling.
The youngest is proclaimed to be red and tawny; when the tail is black in color and the body is white in color, it is Bali.
Having seen such a goat from afar, one should avoid it; likewise, a wise person should always avoid one that is white with a black tail.
A king who desires water should designate a royal beast; he should offer a beautiful animal endowed with all auspicious marks.
For the sake of nourishment, a goat that is aged, large-eared, and complete in all its limbs should be offered; and for the sake of peace, a ram should likewise be given.
One should avoid a man who has missing limbs, extra limbs, is emaciated, or is a child; for one with missing limbs there is poverty, and for one with extra limbs there is an increase in enemies.
If it is in the field, there will be suffering from disease; if in the child, it will take away strength. A white-tailed dog takes away wealth, while a black-tailed dog takes away offspring.
One devoid of horns destroys one's kinsmen; one devoid of ears destroys prosperity; one devoid of eyes destroys longevity; and one afflicted by disease suffers from misery and weakness.
Therefore, O Sovereign of the Gods, having investigated with effort, the animal should be seized; one should first place the Brāhmī mantra at the root of its right ear.
One should perform the five-fold ritual worship (pañcopacāra-pūjā) before the maṇḍala;
thus says Īśvara.
One should worship the supreme hero with groups of goats and offerings; by giving the offering according to the rule, one attains the highest perfection.

One should worship the supreme bali offering with water for the guest (argha) and streams of flowers; O Goddess, one should likewise offer the life-force (prāṇa) as well as a goat and a sheep as the bali.
An offering should not be given by women or eunuchs; having given it, one would encounter obstacles. A person attains success immediately by shaking the offering.
Even by shaking one's head while standing on the ground, one may cause a multitude of obstacles; therefore, with every effort, one should worship Bali according to the prescribed rite.

One should consecrate the sacrificial animal with the mantra of the animal and with that which arises from the Vedas and Tantras; he who always offers the animal [should do so] with the mantra "Rudraḥ khun-ta."
That animal attains heaven who always offers an animal as a sacrifice.
Accompanied by the sacrificial animal, he attains heaven.
89b) Oṃ, one should ask forgiveness from the Blessed One residing within the jar and the maṇḍala: "He who is the one God, the omniscient witness of all action."

Since he is unapproachable even by Brahmā and the other gods, yet is worshipped by me in the sacrifice—the Lord who is both with parts and without parts, established in the station of the twelve-finger space (dvādaśānta).
That divine Lord Śambhu has been troubled by this ritual procedure—he who alone is capable of performing creation, preservation, and destruction.

Śambhu, who possesses three forms and three qualities, was worshipped at the sacrifice by Samayā, just as he was not [so worshipped] by the God of gods, who is beyond qualities and whose form is the Self.
Together with the Śakti, she has been accepted in three ways and worshipped according to the rule at the sacrifice; today my birth has become fruitful, and today my actions have become fruitful.
Such is the power of Śambhu that he has been worshipped by me in this sacrifice; you alone are the Lord himself, the singular savior from saṃsāra.
He alone is the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation, the sole refuge of all; O God, protect me today, who am without a protector, from this peril of sin.
Grant me success, supernatural power, as well as wisdom and mental purity; grant me certainly both worldly enjoyment and liberation, as desired by my mind.
In every way, O Great Lord, grant me here eternal perfection; O Śambhu, O Supreme Lord, grant me the state free from affliction.
Now, O Supreme Lord, may you be forgiven, may you be forgiven, O Master! You have been exerted in this sacrifice; therefore, being satisfied, go to your own abode.
O Śambhu, that man who possesses eternal devotion toward You at all times and in every way throughout all births and actions shall become a partaker of liberation.
Whatever sin was committed by me in a previous birth, or whatever I am committing here in this revolving birth, from that [sin], O Lord Yama, [deliver me].
O Lord, who else but you, the helmsman Śiva, is capable of uplifting me from this ocean of saṃsāra, were it not for these words of mine?
May he, who is intent on removing the most terrible cycle of worldly existence and who bestows supreme bliss, be present for me in birth after birth.
Or rather, O Śiva, by Your grace, even the fear of rebirth does not exist for me; for one whose bonds have been burnt away by initiation, O Lord, whence could there be bondage?

"O All-pervading Lord, my latent impressions (*vāsanā*) are dependent upon the machine of *saṃsāra*; I take refuge in You, the Mantra, and in that Tantra. My intellect lacks the essence of awakening through various scriptures; may my mind be pacified by performing those various virtuous deeds. Having thus asked the Lord for forgiveness, one should dismiss Gaṇeśvara and the other deities.
For example: Gaṇeśa and others are remembered here for the task of guarding the gateway; likewise Indra and the other world-protectors (lokapālas), the Ādityas, or the nine planets;
and those Bhairavas such as Kapāleśa who are supported by the Bhairavīs.
The mantras of the seven enclosures, as well as the deities such as the faces, Vaṭuka and the others, Heruka and the others, and the eternal Kṣetrapālas.
May they all, having bestowed various enjoyments, return to their own abode; O Lord of Gaṇas, Great Fierce One, destroyer of the flood of obstacles!
Accept my worship, O God, whose face is the leader of the hosts; salutations to you, the beloved of the six-faced one, who are honored by the gods with their gestures of reverence.
Accept my worship, O God Kārttikeya; salutations to you! O Mother Lakṣmī, Queen of the three worlds, whose nature is renowned and stainless!
Accept my worship, O Goddess; grant me eternal perfection. O Blessed Lord, O God, you have been distressed by me during the sacrifice.
Accept this worship, O Lord of Gods; may you be forgiven, may you be forgiven, O Lord! O Blessed One, O Blessed Fire, you have been troubled by me at this sacrifice.

O Lord of Gods, accept this worship; O Lord, O Blessed One, Dharmarāja, please forgive me for having troubled you during this sacrifice. O Śiva, accept this worship; O Lord, please forgive me. O Blessed One, Nirṛti, protect me from the terrible ocean of saṃsāra. You have been troubled at the proper time; O Lord, go now to your own abode. O Blessed One, Varuṇa, since you are present in this sacrifice dedicated to the deity Śiva...
"O Lord, you have indeed been troubled by me, for you are the purifier of your own abode; O Blessed One, O Vāyu, you have been troubled at the sacrifice of Śambhu."
Having accepted my worship, you [should perform] the *māyā* [mantra]:
*oṃ śrī gurubhyo namaḥ*. *Oṃ*, I bow with my head to the peaceful True Guru, who is manifest in the form of Śiva, seated upon the *yogapīṭha*.
For the sake of accomplishing the goal of liberation and desire.

I bow to the glorious Guru, supreme bliss, whose form is bliss itself; by whose mere presence the Supreme becomes manifest as consciousness-bliss, using the probe of the ointment of knowledge for one blinded by the darkness of ignorance.
Salutation to that illustrious Guru by whom the eye was opened; he by whom the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings is pervaded in the form of an unbroken circle.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state has been revealed; the Guru alone is the supreme mantra, the Guru alone is the supreme goal.
The Guru alone is the supreme knowledge; there is nothing whatsoever apart from the Guru. The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is Maheśvara himself.
The Guru alone is the entire universe; salutations to that illustrious Guru, who pacifies ignorance and suffering and dries up the ocean of hell.

The guru is the staircase to the door of liberation; O Goddess, the guru is the supreme mantra and the guru alone is the highest goal. One should constantly worship the guru, O Goddess, by which he becomes pleased.
Salutations to you, O Lord, Blessed One, Śiva in the form of the Guru, who has assumed manifold forms for the sake of the perfect accomplishment of the descent of knowledge.
To the ever-new one, whose form is ever-new, who possesses the single form of ultimate reality, and who manifests as a mass of pure consciousness that destroys the darkness of all ignorance.

Salutation to the Supreme Self, who is independent, whose form is fashioned by his own will, yet who is dependent upon his devotees, appearing in auspicious forms for those who are destined for liberation.
To the one who is the form of knowledge for the wise, the light for those who illuminate; the discernment for the discriminating, and the reflective awareness for those possessed of insight.
O Creator, may I always pay homage with my entire being—standing before you, at your sides, behind you, above, and below—granting me your seat.
Oṃ. The Illustrious Goddess said:

Victory, accomplishment, and supernatural power—when the offering is made facing east, O Great Goddess, if there is shaking, then one should predict all these results.
In the northeast, there shall be success in mantra; likewise, in the southeast, victory. In the south, there is the shaking of Bala; one should predict death in the southwest.
In the southwest, it should be known as equal; in the west, it destroys obstacles; in the northwest, there shall be an increase of wealth; and in the north, victory is certain.
Moreover, the deities are pleased elsewhere; indeed, in the east there is much auspiciousness. In the south one meets death, and in the northwest there is expulsion.
In the northeast there is constant prosperity, and in the north there is knowledge. In the southwest there is the death of kinsmen, but in the west there is great fruit.

The killing of animals for one's own sake is violence; in a sacrifice, the killing of an animal is an offering. Thus is the killing of animals declared according to the Vedic and Tantric injunctions.

If there is movement of the head, there is fear of the master; if it occurs at the commencement, there will be danger. If it is fixed, one should know there is fear; O God, some misfortune will arise.

If [the breath] falls on the head, there will be many diseases; if it trembles, calamity is certain. If it falls with urine, there will be a burning sensation from fire; if it falls during Viṣṭi, there is loss of wealth.

If the victory of the gambler comes after that of the royal family, it will be foremost; there will be constant miseries regarding the vehicle and the destruction of the lineage through wandering. Having thus examined these signs, one should observe the great characteristics in those possessing auspicious marks.
